chunks.title: Grounding and Electric Shock Risk
chunks.content: This dishwasher must be properly grounded to reduce electric shock risk. Improper connection of the grounding conductor can result in serious injury or death.

scenarios.condition: Appliance is not properly grounded or grounding conductor is improperly connected
steps: Check with a qualified electrician or authorized service representative.
Ensure the appliance is connected to a metal, permanent wiring system with an equipment grounding conductor.

chunks.title: Hydrogen Gas Explosion Risk
chunks.content: If the hot water system has been unused for two weeks or more, hydrogen gas may accumulate and is explosive. Before running the dishwasher, turn on all hot faucets and let water flow for several minutes to release the gas; do not smoke or use open flames during this time.

scenarios.condition: Hot water system unused for two or more weeks
steps: Turn on all hot water faucets.
Let water flow from each faucet for several minutes to release accumulated hydrogen gas.
Do not smoke or use open flames during this process.
Then proceed to use the dishwasher normally.

chunks.title: Safe Loading of Sharp Utensils
chunks.content: Load knives and other sharp utensils with handles up (in the silverware basket) or edges/points down (in the silverware drawer) to reduce cut injury risk. Do not allow children to handle or play near sharp utensils.

chunks.title: Hot Water and Steam Caution When Opening Door
chunks.content: Always use caution when opening the door during or after a wash cycle, as hot water or steam may escape. Do not fully open the door until water noises have stopped and steam has subsided.

chunks.title: Child Safety
chunks.content: Do not allow children to play in or on the dishwasher. When discarding an old dishwasher, remove the door to the washing compartment to prevent entrapment.

chunks.title: Sanitize Option Warning
chunks.content: Only sanitizing cycles meet the requirements for soil removal and sanitation efficacy. Not all cycles on a certified machine have passed the sanitization performance test.

chunks.title: Technical Specifications
chunks.content: The DWHD640EFM operates at 120V/60Hz with a 1440W power rating and 12A fuse. Load capacity is 16 place settings; water pressure range is 7.25–145 psi; hot water inlet max is 140°F (60°C).

chunks.title: Dishwasher Cycles Overview
chunks.content: Five main cycles are available: Pots & Pans (intensive, 1:50–2:20 hr), Auto (sensor-controlled, 1:45–2:09 hr), Normal (most economical, 2:15–2:35 hr), Hand Wash (gentle, 1:15–1:25 hr), and Quick (30 min). A customizable Favorite cycle can also be saved.

chunks.title: Wash Options
chunks.content: Three options are available: Extra Dry (increases final rinse temp and extends drying, good for plastics), Power Boost (increases lower rack spray pressure for mixed loads), and Sanitize (increases temperature and cycle length; display shows 'SAnI' when complete).

chunks.title: Sensor Settings
chunks.content: Three sensor sensitivity levels (SE:00–SE:02) adjust cycle strength in Auto cycles. SE:00 is optimal for mixed/heavily soiled loads and saves energy; SE:01 adjusts for low soiling; SE:02 is for stubborn dried-on food or ecological detergents.

rows: Optimal for mixed loads and heavily soiled dishware; saves energy and water (factory default)
Adjusts cycle strength for effective removal even at low soiling levels
For difficult conditions or stubborn dried-on food; recommended with ecological detergents

chunks.title: Basic Settings Overview
chunks.content: Basic settings include rinse aid dispenser level (r:00–r:06), sensor setting (SE:00–SE:02), Extra Dry (d:00–d:01), infoLight (I:00–I:01), start cycle default (SP:00–SP:01), signal volume (SL:00–SL:03), button volume (bL:00–bL:03), Wi-Fi (Cn:00–Cn:01), Remote Start (rc:00–rc:02), and factory reset (rE).

chunks.title: Rack Height Settings
chunks.content: Upper rack height can be set to 3 positions. With silverware basket: Setting 1 allows upper rack max ø 24 cm / lower rack 33 cm; Setting 2: 26.5 cm / 30.5 cm; Setting 3: 29 cm / 28 cm. With silverware drawer, upper rack heights are smaller (18, 20.5, 23 cm).

chunks.title: First-Time Setup and Initial Use
chunks.content: Before first use: add rinse aid, add detergent (1–3 tbsp depending on soil level), turn on the appliance, set rinse aid amount, then run the highest-temperature cycle without dishware to remove residues. Connect to the Home Connect® app to access additional cycles and settings.

chunks.title: Starting and Operating a Wash Cycle
chunks.content: Press ON/OFF (1-second touch) to switch on; select a cycle and options; press START/RESUME to begin. The cycle ends when the display shows '00h:00m'. The appliance auto-shuts off 10 minutes after cycle end.

chunks.title: Interrupting and Terminating a Wash Cycle
chunks.content: To pause: press ON/OFF (program is saved); press ON/OFF again then START/RESUME to continue. To cancel a cycle early: open the door, press ON/OFF for ~4 seconds, close the door — residual water pumps out and the cycle ends in ~1 minute.

chunks.title: Loading Dishware Correctly
chunks.content: Remove large food remnants (do not pre-rinse under running water). Place heavily soiled items in the lower rack, position containers opening-down, ensure spray arms can rotate freely, and load silverware with points/edges down. Do not block the detergent dispenser lid.

chunks.title: Removing Dishware After Cycle
chunks.content: Open the door slightly and allow dishes to cool for a few minutes before unloading. Unload starting from the bottom rack upward to prevent water dripping from upper items onto lower ones.

chunks.title: Adding Rinse Aid
chunks.content: When the rinse aid indicator lights up, press the catch on the dispenser lid and lift it, fill to the max mark with household dishwasher rinse aid, wipe up any spills (to prevent excess frothing), and close the lid until it clicks.

chunks.title: Adjusting Rinse Aid Amount
chunks.content: Press ON/OFF, hold Button A for 3 seconds to open basic settings, press A repeatedly until 'r:05' appears, then press START/RESUME to adjust level (r:00 = off, r:01–r:06). Hold Button A for 3 seconds to save. Lower settings reduce streaking; higher settings reduce water spots.

chunks.title: Adjusting Upper Rack Height
chunks.content: Pull out the upper rack, hold the top edge to prevent it dropping, press in both side levers simultaneously, raise or lower the rack evenly to the desired level (check both sides are level), release the levers until they click, then slide the rack back in.

chunks.title: Saving a Favorite Cycle
chunks.content: Open the appliance door, press ON/OFF, press the right cycle button to select a cycle, then press the desired option button — the combination is saved as Favorite. To reset, use the Home Connect app or restore factory settings.

chunks.title: Setting Up Home Connect App
chunks.content: Install the Home Connect® app on your mobile device, start the app and complete registration, then open the app and scan the QR code in the manual to connect the appliance. The appliance must be within range of your home Wi-Fi network.

chunks.title: Changing Basic Settings
chunks.content: Open the door, press ON/OFF, hold Button A for 3 seconds to enter basic settings, press A repeatedly to navigate to the desired setting, press START/RESUME to change the value, then hold Button A for 3 seconds to save. Close the door when done.

chunks.title: Preparing Appliance for Transport
chunks.content: Remove all dishware, secure loose parts, open the water supply valve, switch on the appliance, select the highest-temperature cycle, start it, then terminate after ~4 minutes to drain. Switch off, close the water supply valve, detach the supply hose and let residual water drain. Always transport upright.

chunks.title: Cleaning the Filter System
chunks.content: Check the filters for residues after each dishwashing cycle. Scan the QR code in the manual or visit thermador.com for detailed filter cleaning instructions.

chunks.title: Cleaning the Spray Arms
chunks.content: If dishware is not being washed properly, clean the spray arms by following the instructions accessible via the QR code in the manual. Ensure spray arm nozzles are clear and arms can rotate freely.

chunks.title: Cleaning the Drain Pump
chunks.content: If water no longer drains properly, disconnect power, remove racks and filter system, scoop out water, pry off the pump cover with a spoon, remove food remnants or foreign objects from the impeller area, reinsert and press the cover until it clicks, then reinstall filter and racks.

chunks.title: Preventing Material Damage
chunks.content: Do not use bleach-based products, steam cleaners, abrasive sponges, or stainless steel polish on anti-fingerprint or black stainless finishes. Let the appliance cool before opening the door after a cycle to prevent cabinet damage from steam.

chunks.title: Vacation and Winterizing Preparation
chunks.content: Before vacation in warm weather, turn off the main water valve and the nearest supply valve to the dishwasher. If the appliance will be unused in freezing temperatures for an extended period, have it winterized by a professional service to protect the fill valve.

chunks.title: Error Codes – Water Supply and Drainage
chunks.content: Common water-related error codes and their fixes. E:32-00 indicates a closed water supply valve or kinked/blocked inlet hose; E:34-00 means water is continuously running in; E:61-02 and E:61-03 relate to drain pump blockage or drainage issues.

chunks.content: E:30-00 and E:31-00 indicate the water protection system is activated — close the water supply valve and contact customer service. E:90-01 means power voltage is too low — call an electrician. E:20-60 means the heating element is calcified — descale the appliance.

chunks.title: Error Codes – Electronics and LED Faults
chunks.content: If all LEDs light up or flash, a software update may be installing (wait up to 30 minutes). If the appliance is still not ready, press the main switch for ~4 seconds to reset. If the problem persists, unplug for 2 minutes, then restart; contact service if still unresolved.

chunks.title: Poor Wash Results – Food Remnants on Dishware
chunks.content: Food remnants remaining after a cycle are typically caused by overloading, blocked spray arms, dirty filters, incorrect filter installation, too-light a cycle, or over-pre-cleaning (which causes sensors to select a lighter cycle). Solutions include spacing dishware, cleaning spray arms and filters, and adjusting sensor sensitivity.

chunks.title: Streaks, Spots, and Residue on Dishware
chunks.content: Streaks on glassware are usually caused by too much rinse aid; water spots by too little. Detergent residue in the dispenser or collecting tray is caused by blocked spray arms or a damp dispenser. Rust spots on silverware indicate non-rust-resistant items or washing with rusting items.

tasks.title: Check and Clean the Filter System
tasks.description: Inspect and clean the dishwasher filters after every wash cycle to remove food debris.
tasks.justification: Clogged filters cause poor wash results, drainage problems, and can damage the pump.
tasks.instructions_text: After each cycle, remove the lower rack and lift out the filter system. Rinse the filters under running water to remove food debris. Reinstall the filters and twist them into place until they click. Scan the QR code in the manual (section 14.1) for a detailed video guide.

tasks.title: Clean the Spray Arms
tasks.description: Clean the upper and lower spray arms when dishware is not being washed properly.
tasks.justification: Blocked spray arm nozzles prevent water from reaching dishware, resulting in poor cleaning performance.
tasks.instructions_text: If dishes are coming out dirty, check that the spray arms can rotate freely and that no dishware is blocking them. Remove the spray arms and rinse the nozzles under running water to clear any blockages. Scan the QR code in section 14.2 of the manual for a detailed video guide.

tasks.title: Clean the Drain Pump
tasks.description: Clear food remnants or foreign objects from the drain pump when water is no longer draining properly.
tasks.justification: A blocked drain pump prevents water from draining and can damage the pump motor.
tasks.instructions_text: Disconnect the appliance from power. Remove upper and lower racks and the filter system. Scoop out any standing water with a sponge. Pry the pump cover off with a spoon, grip it by the crosspiece, and lift it diagonally inward. Remove any food remnants or foreign objects from the impeller area. Reinsert the pump cover and press down until it clicks. Reinstall the filter system and racks. Use caution — there may be sharp debris such as glass fragments.

tasks.title: Descale the Appliance
tasks.description: Descale the dishwasher when error code E:20-60 appears, indicating the heating element is calcified.
tasks.justification: Mineral scale buildup on the heating element reduces efficiency and can cause the element to fail.
tasks.instructions_text: When error code E:20-60 appears, run a descaling cycle using a dishwasher-safe descaling product. Follow the descaling product's instructions for dosage and cycle selection. After descaling, consider using the water softening system (if available on your model) to prevent future buildup.

tasks.title: Refill the Rinse Aid Dispenser
tasks.description: Refill the rinse aid dispenser when the rinse aid refill indicator lights up.
tasks.justification: Without rinse aid, dishware will have water spots and drying performance will be significantly reduced.
tasks.instructions_text: When the rinse aid indicator lights up on the control panel, press the catch on the dispenser lid and lift it open. Pour household dishwasher rinse aid up to the max mark. Wipe up any spills immediately (spilled rinse aid causes excess frothing). Close the lid until it clicks into position.

tasks.title: Winterize the Appliance
tasks.description: Have the dishwasher professionally winterized if it will be unused in freezing temperatures for an extended period.
tasks.justification: Freezing temperatures can damage the fill valve, and this damage is not covered by the warranty.
tasks.instructions_text: If the dishwasher will be unused in a location with freezing temperatures (e.g., a vacation home), arrange for a professional service technician to winterize the appliance. For warm-weather vacations, turn off the main water valve and the nearest supply valve to the dishwasher before leaving.

tasks.title: Run Initial Empty Cycle
tasks.description: Run the highest-temperature cycle without dishware before first use to remove manufacturing residues.
tasks.justification: Running an empty cycle removes water marks and residues from the manufacturing process before washing dishware.
tasks.instructions_text: Add rinse aid and detergent. Turn on the appliance and set the rinse aid amount. Select the cycle with the highest cleaning temperature (Pots & Pans). Press START/RESUME and run the full cycle without any dishware inside.

tasks.title: Verify Grounding and Electrical Connection
tasks.description: Confirm the dishwasher is properly grounded to a metal, permanent wiring system before first use.
tasks.justification: Improper grounding can result in electric shock in the event of a malfunction or breakdown.
tasks.instructions_text: Verify with a qualified electrician that the appliance is connected to a properly grounded circuit. The appliance must be grounded to a metal, permanent wiring system or have an equipment grounding conductor run with the circuit conductors. Refer to the Installation Instructions for full electrical requirements.

re_check_triggers.description: You notice sparks, burning smell, or receive a shock when touching the appliance

weekly.title: Weekly Cleaning
steps: Check and clean the filter system — remove, rinse under running water, and reinstall.
Wipe down the door seal and interior edges with a damp cloth to remove food debris.
Check that spray arms rotate freely and nozzles are not blocked.
Wipe the exterior and control panel with a soft, damp cloth — do not use abrasive cleaners or bleach-based products.

deep_clean.title: Deep Clean
steps: Remove and thoroughly clean the filter system under running water, using a soft brush if needed.
Remove the spray arms and rinse nozzles under running water to clear mineral deposits or food debris.
If error code E:20-60 appears, run a descaling cycle using a dishwasher-safe descaling product.
Clean the drain pump if water is not draining properly — disconnect power, remove racks and filter, scoop water, remove pump cover, clear impeller, and reassemble.
Wipe the interior tub walls and door interior with a damp cloth.
Check the rinse aid dispenser and refill if the indicator is lit.
